title: Bulbar urethroplasty with buccal mucosa graft
subtitle: Open the stricture fully, then augment with a quilted buccal graft

sources.title: BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: A bulbar urethral stricture too long for excision and primary anastomosis, or recurrent after urethrotomy.
contraindications: Active lichen sclerosus in the mouth or oral disease at the donor site.
preparation: Retrograde and voiding urethrogram for length and site; cystoscopy.
Suprapubic catheter in place if the patient was in retention.
Consent: recurrence, mouth pain and numbness, erectile and ejaculatory change, urinary dribbling, wound problems.
positioning: Lithotomy with legs well supported and padded; nasal intubation so the mouth is free.
equipment: Urethroplasty set, ring retractor, bougies, fine absorbable sutures, guidewire, cystoscope, buccal harvest set with mouth gag.
anatomy: Bulbar urethra and corpus spongiosum, bulbospongiosus muscle, corpora cavernosa; in the cheek, Stensen's duct and the mental nerve near the lip.
criticalSafety: Open the urethra into healthy calibre at both ends.
Keep the harvest away from Stensen's duct opening.
commonErrors: A graft that does not lie flat on a bed.
postop: Catheter about 2 to 3 weeks; pericatheter urethrogram before removal.
Flow rate and symptom checks; urethrogram if symptoms return.

steps.emphasis: Mouth donor site and recurrence discussed.
Lithotomy, legs well padded and limited in time; nasal tube so the mouth is free.
Perineum prepared; the mouth prepared separately with its own instruments.
Look at the stricture and pass a wire into the bladder if possible.
Catheter stays 2 to 3 weeks; urethrogram before removal.
Check the spongiosum edges and the cheek.
Close bulbospongiosus and the perineum in layers.
Record stricture length, graft size and position, and the urethrogram date.

step.urp.harvest.title: Harvest the buccal graft
step.urp.harvest.why: Inner cheek mucosa is wet, thick and takes well. Staying away from the duct and the lip keeps the mouth healthy.
how: Open the mouth with a gag, mark Stensen's duct opening (opposite the second upper molar) and stay below it.
Mark a graft about 1.5 to 2.5 cm wide and as long as needed; inject local anaesthetic with adrenaline.
Take the mucosa only, thin the graft of fat on the back table; close or leave the cheek per preference.

step.urp.expose.title: Expose the bulbar urethra
step.urp.expose.why: A midline perineal approach with the bulbospongiosus split gives access to the whole bulbar urethra.
how: Make a midline or inverted-Y perineal incision.
Split the bulbospongiosus muscle in the midline to show the corpus spongiosum.
Mobilise the urethra as needed for the graft (dorsal or ventral).

step.urp.open.title: Open the stricture into healthy urethra
step.urp.open.why: Recurrence comes from scar left at the ends. The stricture is opened until healthy calibre is seen at both ends.
how: Open the urethra along the stricture (dorsal or ventral stricturotomy).
Extend the opening beyond the stricture at both ends until a 24 to 26 Fr bougie passes easily.
Measure the length of the opened urethra for the graft.
pitfalls: Stopping in scar at either end.

step.urp.graft.title: Quilt and sew the graft
step.urp.graft.why: The graft lives on its bed in the first days. Quilting it flat and fixing it on all sides lets it take.
how: Lay the graft on its bed (corpora dorsally or spongiosum ventrally) and quilt it with fine sutures so it lies flat.
Sew the urethral edges to the graft over a catheter with fine absorbable sutures, apex first.
Close the spongiosum over the graft where possible.
pitfalls: A loose graft with fluid under it.
